perOption.label: (A)
perOption.reason: "Garcia stood outside..., waiting for his brother" — present-participle adjunct whose understood subject is Garcia (the one waiting). Standard narrative construction; no dangling-modifier issue. No real distractor pull.

perOption.label: (B)
perOption.reason: "they're a bit too colorful" refers back to "a patterned red shirt and yellow pants" — a coordinated plural antecedent (and "pants" is plural on its own). Plural pronoun is required and used. Checked for a singular-antecedent trap; none exists.

perOption.label: (C)
perOption.reason: "he struggled with the rhythm, making several mistakes" — participial adjunct, subject = he, expressing accompanying result. Grammatical and parallel in form to (A).

perOption.label: (D)
perOption.reason: "Garcia's trumpet playing was flawlessly." The copula "was" takes an adjectival subject complement: it must be "flawless." An adverb cannot function as predicate complement. Actively tested a rescue parse (ellipsis of a participle, e.g. "was flawlessly [performed]") — no such ellipsis is licensed; as written the sentence is ungrammatical. Adjective-vs-adverb after a linking verb is the governing rule.

perOption.label: (E)
perOption.reason: "When the band was finished" — genuine attractor: a solver may want active "had finished" and suspect a passive misuse. But "be finished" is a standard adjectival/resultative use meaning "done" (cf. "I'm finished"), fully grammatical with an agentive subject. Felt the pull, rejected it.

note: Clean single-answer item. (D) is unambiguously wrong by the linking-verb + adjective-complement rule; the strongest distractor is (E) (be finished vs. had finished), which is grammatically sound on the adjectival reading. No alternative parse rescues (D). Difficulty modest for a top-tier examinee — the D/E pair is the intended discrimination point.
